cards.title: The bent straw
cards.idea: A straw in a glass of water looks broken at the surface. Nothing touched it — only the light path changed as it crossed into water.

interaction.prompt: Tap the exact spot on the straw where it appears to bend.

cards.reveal: You tapped the water surface. Light bends there because it enters a new medium, and your eye traces it back to the wrong place.

cards.title: Crossing the boundary
cards.idea: A light ray travels from air into water. Watch how its direction changes at the surface, not before or after.

interaction.prompt: Slide to change the angle of the incoming ray from air into water.

cards.reveal: A bigger incoming angle gives a bigger bend. Going air to water, the ray always bends toward the normal, the line perpendicular to the surface.

cards.title: Fast to slow, and back
cards.idea: Light moves slower in water and glass than in air. Speed change is why the ray turns at the boundary.

interaction.prompt: Drag the ray so it exits water back into air, and predict its new direction.

cards.reveal: Water to air: light speeds up and bends away from the normal. Denser medium slows light and bends it toward the normal.

cards.title: Naming it
cards.idea: Refraction is the bending of light when it passes from one transparent medium into another because its speed changes.

interaction.prompt: Type the word for the bending of light as it changes medium.

cards.reveal: Refraction. Toward the normal entering a denser medium, away from the normal entering a rarer one. No speed change means no bending.

cards.title: When it does not bend
cards.idea: A ray hitting the surface head-on, straight along the normal, passes through without bending at all.

interaction.prompt: Tap the incoming ray that will pass straight through with no bending.

cards.reveal: The ray along the normal, at 0 degrees, goes straight. Refraction needs the ray to strike at an angle to the surface.

workbook.prompt: When light passes from air into water, it bends
The bending of light as it moves from one transparent medium to another is called ________.
A straw in water looks broken because
options: light bends at the water surface
workbook.answer: light bends at the water surface

boss.prompt: Light travels from glass back into air. Compared to inside the glass, it
options: slows down and bends toward the normal
speeds up and bends away from the normal
keeps the same speed and direction
boss.answer: speeds up and bends away from the normal

boss.prompt: A ray entering a denser medium exactly along the normal bends by ________ degrees.
Which change is the real cause of refraction at a boundary?
options: the change in the speed of light
the change in the colour of light
the change in the brightness of light
boss.answer: the change in the speed of light
